title: Training in translation tools and technologies: Findings of the EMT survey 2023
abstract: arXiv:2503.22735v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: This article reports on the third iteration of a survey of computerized tools and technologies taught as part of postgraduate translation training programmes. While the survey was carried out under the aegis of the EMT Network, more than half of responses are from outside that network. The results show the responsiveness of programmes to innovations in translation technology, with increased compulsory inclusion of machine translation, post-editing, and quality evaluation, and a rapid response to the release of generative tools. The flexibility required during the Covid-19 pandemic has also led to some lasting changes to programmes. While the range of tools being taught has continued to expand, programmes seem to be consolidating their core offering around cloud-based software with cost-free academic access. translated_title: 翻译工具与技术培训：2023年EMT调查结果
translated_abstract: 本文报告了针对研究生翻译培养项目中教授的计算机化工具与技术的第三次调查结果。尽管该调查是在EMT网络的支持下开展的，但超过半数的回复来自该网络之外。结果显示，各培养项目对翻译技术创新反应迅速，机器翻译、译后编辑和质量评估越来越多地被纳入必修内容，并对生成式工具的发布做出了快速响应。新冠疫情期间所需的灵活性也给培养项目带来了一些持久性的变化。尽管所教授的工具范围不断扩大，各项目似乎正在围绕可免费获取学术授权的云端软件来整合其核心教学内容。此外，与翻译技术相关的专业情境和工作流程在教学中的融入程度也有所提升。
tldr: 2023年EMT调查显示，翻译技术教学正快速响应行业创新：机器翻译、译后编辑与质量评估日益成为必修内容，培养项目对生成式AI工具反应迅速，并趋向以免费学术授权的云端软件为核心整合教学体系。
en_tdlr: The 2023 EMT survey reveals that translation programmes are rapidly adapting to technological innovation, with increasing compulsory inclusion of machine translation, post-editing, and quality evaluation, fast uptake of generative AI tools, and consolidation of core teaching around cloud-based software with free academic access.
